# src/lease.ts — cross-process write-ownership lock (excerpt)

> Cross-process write-ownership lock for one session's artifact directory,
> held for the whole life of a write handle. The arbiter is the kernel:
> POSIX takes a non-blocking `flock(2)` (through fs-ext) on `session.lock`
> beside the log, and **Windows holds a named kernel semaphore derived from
> that path — never a file lock or handle**, so readers, searches, and
> directory removal proceed freely while the lock is held. …

```ts
import { flock } from 'fs-ext'
import { acquireLockHandleWin32, releaseLockHandleWin32 } from './win32.ts'
```

> … **Windows has no lock file at all.** Readers never touch the lock. …

Note: `flock` is imported statically at module top — the package loader must
resolve and load `fs-ext` even on Windows, where the `flock` branch is never
taken.

references.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 · Windows install fails on the `fs-ext` native build; the runtime never calls `flock` on Windows

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers / packaging; any Windows machine without Visual Studio
  Build Tools upgrading to 0.1.3-alpha.1
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/install surface)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `pnpm install` exits 1. `fs-ext@2.1.1` runs its `node-gyp configure build`
  install script and fails with `gyp ERR! find VS … You need to install the latest version of
  Visual Studio (including the "Desktop development with C++" workload)`. `fs-ext` is a pinned
  dependency of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` and is statically imported from
  `src/lease.ts`, so `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` cannot skip it — the module must exist
  and load.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Confirm the platform path first: on Windows, `lease.ts` takes `acquireLockHandleWin32`
     (a named kernel semaphore via `CreateSemaphoreW`) and holds "never a file lock or
     handle"; `flock` is only the POSIX branch. The native module is dead code on Windows.
  2. Add a pnpm patch (the repository already patches native packages this way, e.g.
     `patches/node-pty@*`): rewrite the install script to run `node-gyp` only on non-Windows,
     and give the entry a pure-JS `flock` fallback (warn once, no-op). Linux/macOS keep the
     native build.
  3. Register the patch in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`patchedDependencies` and `allowBuilds`)
     and re-run `pnpm install`.
  Do not install Visual Studio just for this, do not patch upstream, and do not rely on
  `--ignore-scripts` alone.
- **Verification**: `pnpm install` completes; `require('fs-ext')` loads and the flock callback
  path warns once instead of throwing; `dsh web --no-open` boots and answers HTTP 200.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1)
  (`d347e70`): `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/package.json` pins `"fs-ext": "2.1.1"`;
  `src/lease.ts` statically imports `flock` from `fs-ext` and routes Windows through
  `acquireLockHandleWin32`; `src/win32.ts` carries the named-semaphore bindings ·
  single-host field report (Windows 11 without MSVC, 2026-09-07)

candidate_reports.S20-msvc-flock-trap/report.md:
# S20 · Windows Install Blocker — Diagnosis and Fix Plan

## 1. What fails, and why

- **Failing package/step**: `fs-ext@2.1.1` fails during its `install` script, which runs `node-gyp configure build` (`install-error.log:3`).
- **Package origin**: `fs-ext@2.1.1` is a pinned runtime dependency of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl@0.1.3-alpha.1`, declared in `manifest-excerpt.json:5`.
- **Root cause**: node-gyp cannot find a C++ toolchain: `gyp ERR! find VS msvs_version not set…`, `VCINSTALLDIR not set`, and `Could not find any Visual Studio installation to use … "Desktop development with C++" workload` (`install-error.log:4-11`). The machine has no Visual Studio / Build Tools (`README.md:3-4`), so the native build of `fs-ext` can never succeed, and `pnpm install` exits 1 (`install-error.log:12-14`).

## 2. Why `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` cannot fix this

`--ignore-scripts` only skips the `node-gyp` build. It does not remove the dependency: `src/lease.ts` statically imports `flock` from `'fs-ext'` at module top (`lease-excerpt.md:11`), and the loader must resolve and load `fs-ext` even on Windows, where the `flock` branch is never taken (`lease-excerpt.md:17-19`). Skipping the build leaves no loadable native binding, so the module either fails to exist or throws on load — the service cannot boot.

## 3. Which lock path Windows actually takes at runtime

On Windows, `lease.ts` acquires the cross-process write-ownership lock through `acquireLockHandleWin32`/`releaseLockHandleWin32` (`lease-excerpt.md:12`), which wrap native named-semaphore primitives: `CreateSemaphoreW`, `WaitForSingleObject`, `ReleaseSemaphore`, plus `MoveFileExW` (`win32-excerpt.ts:8-13,23-24`). Windows holds **no lock file and no file handle** — it holds a named kernel semaphore derived from the session path (`lease-excerpt.md:6-8,15`). `flock` is invoked only on the POSIX branch. Therefore the failing `fs-ext` native module is dead code on Windows: it is never called, only loaded.

## 4. Concrete, least-invasive fix plan (no Visual Studio, no upstream changes)

Follow the repository's existing `patchedDependencies` precedent (`patches/node-pty@*.patch`, `README.md:7-10`):

1. Create `patches/fs-ext@2.1.1.patch` that rewrites the `fs-ext` package:
   - Replace its `install` script so `node-gyp configure build` runs only on non-Windows platforms (e.g. gate on `process.platform !== 'win32'`); on Windows it exits 0 as a no-op.
   - Replace the entry point with a pure-JS fallback: a `flock` (and friends) implementation that on Windows warns once and no-ops, preserving the exported API shape so the static import in `lease.ts` resolves and loads. Non-Windows keeps the native build and real implementation.
2. Register the patch in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` under `patchedDependencies` (e.g. `"fs-ext@2.1.1": "patches/fs-ext@2.1.1.patch"`), mirroring the existing node-pty entry.
3. Re-run `pnpm install` on the Windows machine: the fs-ext install script no longer invokes node-gyp, so the install completes without MSVC; the patched entry file lets `require('fs-ext')` load fine.
4. Verify: `pnpm install` exits 0; `require('fs-ext')` loads and `flock` warns once instead of throwing; the service boots (e.g. `dsh web --no-open` serves HTTP 200). On POSIX machines the native build still runs, so behavior is unchanged there.

Do not install Visual Studio, do not modify upstream `fs-ext`, do not rely on `--ignore-scripts`.

## 5. Corridor card

`DSH-0.1.3-A1-03` — "Windows install fails on the `fs-ext` native build; the runtime never calls `flock` on Windows" (`references/v0.1.3-alpha.1.md:130`, cross-referenced in `references/troubleshooting.md:21`).
